sources.title: Docker: What is an image?
sources.supportRationale: Images package a runtime filesystem/configuration while containers are running instances with isolation boundaries.

sources.title: Docker: Build best practices

sources.title: Docker: Build secrets
sources.supportRationale: Secret mounts avoid treating build arguments or copied credentials as safe secret storage.

sources.title: Docker: Volumes
sources.supportRationale: Persistent volume ownership differs from a container's writable layer and lifecycle.

sources.title: Docker Engine security
sources.supportRationale: Shared-kernel namespaces/cgroups and daemon privileges define container threat boundaries.

sources.title: Google SRE: Addressing cascading failures
sources.supportRationale: Retry amplification and resource exhaustion spread failures.

sources.title: GitHub Actions: security hardening
sources.supportRationale: Untrusted inputs, action provenance and credential scope constrain workflow execution.

scenarios.theme: Two machines deploy the same tag but behave differently. What do you compare?
scenarios.assumptions: Production and staging both declare the api:latest tag. Their serving behavior differs after a registry update. What will you do?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Docker & Containerization to mutable tag.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Two machines deploy the same tag but behave differently. What do you compare?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Inspect actual image identities and target platforms, compare configuration and dependencies, then deploy the same verified artifact identity through promo

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: A digest proves selected content identity, not that it is safe or correctly configured

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Platform-specific variants and runtime secrets can still differ; locking a vulnerable image forever is not a maintenance strategy.

scenarios.theme: A token was copied then removed in the next build step. Is rotation necessary?
scenarios.assumptions: The image was pushed to a shared registry and a build log printed the token. What response and prevention fit?

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Docker & Containerization to layer secret.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A token was copied then removed in the next build step. Is rotation necessary?

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Treat the credential as exposed, revoke/rotate it and inspect where it propagated

scenarios.theme: Replacing a container loses customer uploads. What storage contract is missing?
scenarios.assumptions: The service writes under its local filesystem and deployment recreates containers. Customers expect files to survive. What changes?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Docker & Containerization to lost uploads.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Replacing a container loses customer uploads. What storage contract is missing?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Move durable objects to an explicitly managed volume/object store or database with appropriate ownership, availability and tested backup/restore

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: A mounted volume changes lifetime, not application-level consistency or cross-host portability

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Sharing one directory between writers may introduce races; storage access and recovery semantics must match the workload.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to volumes, image; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: The container is repeatedly killed under load although the host has spare memory. What next?
scenarios.assumptions: A runtime memory limit is below the application’s peak working set and no graceful error appears. What evidence and change fit?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Docker & Containerization to oom limit.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: The container is repeatedly killed under load although the host has spare memory. What next?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Inspect termination reason, measured working set and limits, reduce unnecessary retention or tune concurrency and runtime memory settings, then adjust the

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Simply removing limits can move failure to other workloads or the host

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Container memory accounting includes more than a language heap; an OOM kill is not equivalent to an application exception with cleanup.

scenarios.theme: A build helper requests the host Docker socket. Is it an ordinary file mount?
scenarios.assumptions: Untrusted build code would reach a daemon that can start privileged host containers. What boundary will you choose?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Docker & Containerization to socket privilege.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A build helper requests the host Docker socket. Is it an ordinary file mount?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Treat daemon access as substantial host authority, isolate untrusted build execution and avoid exposing the privileged socket

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Running as a non-root user inside the helper does not neutralize powerful daemon access

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Stronger isolation costs setup and resources; ordinary shared-kernel containers are not interchangeable with VM boundaries.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to dockersec, ghasec; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A fast rebuild still contains an old vulnerable library. What policy is missing?
scenarios.assumptions: Cached build layers and a stable base identity keep reproducing the same old runtime after a security fix is published. What will you do?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A fast rebuild still contains an old vulnerable library. What policy is missing?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Update reviewed base/dependency inputs, rebuild and verify a new artifact, then promote it with provenance and compatibility checks

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Disabling all cache can increase time without updating pinned inputs

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Reproducibility and deliberate patch freshness need complementary processes.
